svg.aria-label: tee-signer: how it keeps a BTCPay hot wallet out of one login's reach
svg.title: tee-signer — how it keeps a BTCPay hot wallet out of one login's reach
svg.text: A Bitcoin key sealed in an SGX enclave + a mandate signed by the owner
The BIP39 seed sits in NBXplorer's database
An admin login, a plugin or a web-app bug
can read it and sign any transaction
November 2026: hot wallets swept this way
A seed sealed in an enclave
The enclave judges every payout itself.
No seed file: BTCPay keeps a watch-only xpub
Every payout is checked against the owner's
A stolen admin login gets one window's budget
Signed by the owner. Enforced by the enclave, not by BTCPay.
A window is 144 blocks of verified headers, so a host that
moves its clock cannot reset the budget.
Sealed in the enclave on the server
never leaves the enclave in clear
Works unattended: no button, no person
A cold encrypted keyfile, two media
Cancels a pending change, replaces a
lost owner key, opens the recovery blob
The BTCPay server never holds the owner key: whoever controls BTCPay cannot widen its own limits.
the seed out of root's reach
not for money: root reads it
Signet only. Reviewed round by round by an internal AI auditor; not a third-party audit.
